title: Effects of screentime on the health and well-being of children and adolescents: a systematic review of reviews
summary: objectives : to systematically examine the evidence for and harms of screentime in children and young people.methods:we searched electronic databases for systematic reviews of evidence on screentime effects . <n> we included studies published in english between january 1 , 2000 and december 31 , 2015.results:we identified eight studies . screentime was associated with symptoms of depression , anxiety , social support , physical activity , sleep , quality of life , and healthy eating . on average , <n> children and adolescents were exposed to screentime for 3 h per day , including weekends , school recesses , sport , computer use , television , video games , outdoors , on the internet , in front of a computer , or on the computer alone.conclusions:the evidence suggests that screentime is associated with poorer health and well - being .
key_findings: Screentime is associated with symptoms of depression and anxiety in children and adolescents.
Increased screentime correlates with lower levels of physical activity and quality of life.
Children and adolescents are exposed to an average of 3 hours of screentime per day.
methodology: We conducted a systematic review by searching electronic databases for systematic reviews published in English from January 1, 2000, to December 31, 2015.
limitations: The review only included studies published in English.
The studies analyzed were limited to a specific time frame (2000-2015).
Potential biases in the included studies may affect the overall conclusions.
future_work: Investigate the long-term effects of screentime on mental health.
Explore interventions to reduce screentime among children and adolescents.
Examine the impact of different types of screentime on health outcomes.
